description:
The published package contains the generated leex/yecc output (`src/flatbuffer_schema_lexer.erl`, `src/flatbuffer_schema_parser.erl`) even though the repo deliberately ignores them via `src/.gitignore` — only `.xrl`/`.yrl` are tracked.

## Evidence

A clean fetch of the published package delivers files that do not exist in git:

    $ mix deps.get                       # flatbuffer 0.3.1 from hexpm
    $ ls deps/flatbuffer/src/
    flatbuffer_schema_lexer.erl          # <- gitignored upstream, shipped anyway
    flatbuffer_schema_lexer.xrl
    flatbuffer_schema_parser.erl         # <- same
    flatbuffer_schema_parser.yrl

    $ git ls-files src/                  # in this repo
    src/.gitignore
    src/flatbuffer_schema_lexer.xrl
    src/flatbuffer_schema_parser.yrl

## Cause

`package:` in mix.exs declares no `files:` key, so Hex falls back to its default
list, which includes `src`. `mix hex.publish` therefore sweeps in whatever
generated `.erl` happens to be sitting in `src/` from the maintainer's last local
compile.

Still present on main at 0.4.1.

## Why it matters

The published parser is not reproducible from the grammars in the repo. Its
content depends on the leex/yecc (OTP) version the maintainer had installed at
publish time, not on anything under version control.

Worse, leex/yecc only regenerate when the `.erl` is stale relative to the
grammar. A working tree whose `.erl` is newer than an edited `.xrl` — a rebase,
a touch, a clock skew — publishes the OLD parser alongside the NEW grammar, and
consumers compile the stale one. The grammar in git would say one thing and the
shipped package would do another, with nothing in CI to catch the divergence.

## Fix

Add an explicit `files:` list to `package:` that ships the grammars and excludes
the generated output, e.g.

    package: [
      files: ~w(lib src/*.xrl src/*.yrl mix.exs README.md LICENSE.txt),
      ...
    ]

Consumers already declare `compilers: [:yecc, :leex] ++ Mix.compilers()`, which
this project sets, so the grammars regenerate on the consumer side. Verified: a
clean `mix deps.compile flatbuffer` builds `flatbuffer_schema_lexer.beam` and
`flatbuffer_schema_parser.beam` correctly, so removing the prebuilt `.erl` does
not break the build.

Worth also confirming the tarball is otherwise clean (`mix hex.build` then
inspect) while adding the list.

## Not the same as

Found while chasing a bedrock build failure (`:flatbuffer_schema_lexer.string/1
is undefined` during `mix compile --force`). That turned out to be a stale local
`_build` state in bedrock, NOT a defect in the published package — 0.3.1 builds
correctly from a clean fetch. This ticket is the packaging issue found along the
way, which is real and independent.
title: Hex tarball ships generated src/*.erl, which the repo gitignores
